statement: Let n = len(nums), and for 0 <= l <= r <= n let S(l,r) = sum_{k=l}^{r-1} nums[k]. The function returns a result ans such that: (1) if there is no pair (l,r) with 0 <= l < r <= n and S(l,r) >= target, then ans = 0; (2) if there is such a pair, then ans >= 1, there exists a pair (l0,r0) with 0 <= l0 < r0 <= n, r0-l0 = ans, and S(l0,r0) >= target, and for every pair (l,r) with 0 <= l < r <= n and S(l,r) >= target, r-l >= ans.
preconditions: target and nums satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= target <= 10^9; 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^4. All Std.I64 values are interpreted as mathematical integers in their range.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a successful result ans; in particular, it does not fail due to overflow, out-of-bounds access, or a panic.
preconditions: target and nums satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= target <= 10^9; 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^4. All Std.I64 values are interpreted as mathematical integers in their range.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result ans, 0 <= ans <= len(nums).
preconditions: target and nums satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= target <= 10^9; 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^4. All Std.I64 values are interpreted as mathematical integers in their range.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result ans, ans = 0 if and only if sum_{k=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[k] < target.
preconditions: target and nums satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= target <= 10^9; 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^4. All Std.I64 values are interpreted as mathematical integers in their range.

preconditions: target and nums satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= target <= 10^9; 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^4. All Std.I64 values are interpreted as mathematical integers in their range.

preconditions: target and nums satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= target <= 10^9; 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^4. All Std.I64 values are interpreted as mathematical integers in their range.

preconditions: target and nums satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= target <= 10^9; 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^4. All Std.I64 values are interpreted as mathematical integers in their range.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result ans, ans = len(nums) if and only if sum_{k=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[k] >= target and for every pair (l,r) with 0 <= l < r <= len(nums) and (l,r) != (0,len(nums)), sum_{k=l}^{r-1} nums[k] < target.

statement: Let ans1 and ans2 be the results returned by min_sub_array_len on (target1, nums) and (target2, nums), respectively. Whenever these results are returned, the following holds: if ans1 = 0 then ans2 = 0; and if ans2 > 0 then ans1 > 0 and ans1 <= ans2.
preconditions: All mentioned inputs satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= target1 <= 10^9 and 1 <= target2 <= 10^9; the shared slice nums satisfies 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5 and 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^4 for every 0 <= i < len(nums); and target1 <= target2. All Std.I64 values are interpreted as mathematical integers in their range.
